findings.title: Custom logo renders blurry on high-DPI (Retina) displays
findings.description: Customer reported the custom onboarding logo looks soft/blurry on a MacBook with a high-resolution (Retina) display, while it renders fine on a colleague's standard-resolution laptop, matching a low-resolution image being upscaled for high pixel-density screens. The logo's source is a vector file (Illustrator) but the team had exported and uploaded it small (customer estimated ~200px wide), so resolution was not actually constrained on their end. Support asked the customer to re-export the logo at high resolution from the original vector and re-upload under Settings > Branding, with a hard refresh, before treating it as a platform defect. The call ended before the customer confirmed whether the re-upload fixed the rendering, so no platform-side defect was established; the stated cause was a customer-side low-resolution export.
findings.quote: On my MacBook. The new one, the high-resolution display. I open the dashboard and our logo, our beautiful logo that our design team agonized over, looks soft. Fuzzy.
findings.severity_reason: Purely cosmetic rendering issue on one high-DPI device, not confirmed as a platform defect, and a customer-side fix (higher-res re-upload) was already in progress by end of call.
findings.match_note: No catalogue issue covers logo/branding image rendering; distinct from any tracked bug, and root cause points to customer's own low-res export rather than a product defect.

findings.title: Ad-hoc engagement/ROI one-pager requested for leadership readout
findings.description: Customer's managing partner is questioning whether the program spend is worth it, and the customer asked for a clear, presentable answer to bring back to leadership. Rather than pointing to an existing in-product report, the internal CSM offered to manually compile a one-page summary covering utilization, active users, session volume, and trend over the contract term, to be delivered outside the product. This was handled as a support/account-management service action rather than a request to add or fix a product capability, and no specific in-product reporting gap was described.
findings.quote: My managing partner asks whether the spend is worth it and I'd like a crisp answer. Ideally next to a crisp logo.
findings.severity_reason: Not a product defect or feature gap; it is a one-off manual reporting favor performed by the CSM outside the product.
findings.match_note: Superficially adjacent to PROJ-118 (PDF export of engagement summary from manager dashboard), but here the customer never asks for an in-product export capability — the CSM proactively offers a manual, out-of-band deliverable instead.
